reason: The word selon is divided at the line end (ſe-|lon); the hyphen is the expected sign of division and the sense is the same either way.
Calliſtrat = Callistratus, the jurist of D. 22.5.3 whom Coras is quoting; Callittrat is no name.
The sentence continues (Iurisconsulte, poursuyuant l'argument d'Adrian...); a comma, not a full stop, fits the syntax.
c'est à mon aduis, ce que... is one clause; a comma suits it, a semicolon would sever the relative from its antecedent.
veuë matches the same formula printed on p098 (Soit veuë l'annotation xxx.); both spellings give veue and translate alike.
Point or colon after Diuus at the end of a marginal note; the citation and its translation are the same.
Both readings are the same wrong sort for commettent; medial s is set as long ſ in this print, so commeſtẽt is the likelier form; the translation is unaffected.
l. or l before j & ij. D. de legib.: the siglum lex with or without its point; the citation is the same.
{k}, with a single comma; a point followed by a comma after the marker is an unlikely setting, and the clause continues (se pardonne aisement); the translation is the same.
ſ'excuſent, reflexive: the involuntary crimes are those which 'are excused' by chance, error or ignorance; l'excuſent would want an object the sentence does not supply.
beſte = beste, 'beast' (cheureul, sanglier, ou autre beste sauuage); belte is no word, a misread of long ſ as l.
Comma or none after exemple before Si i'ay volonté; punctuation only, translation unaffected.
pa-|pes with lower- or upper-case p in the margin; the word is papes either way.
allegué or allegue, the acute accent on the final e; the word and the citation are the same.
l. or l before Aqui. in the margin: the siglum lex with or without its point; the citation is the same.
finemq́; or finemq;: the -que abbreviation with or without the acute on the q; the word is finemque either way.
ſous la collation vij = 'under the seventh collation' of the Authenticum; ta is a misread of l as t and makes no sense.
Philippenſ. = Philippians (c. i, the chapter cited); Philippexſ. is no word.
The word sapientia is divided across two margin lines (ſa-|pientia); a hyphen is the likelier sign, a point would make nonsense; the citation is the same either way.
pieria and pietia are both wrong sorts for the -pientia of sapientia (Lactantius, De falsa sapientia); nothing in the context favours one misprint over the other.
Sicculíque or Sicculique: the accent on the i before the enclitic -que; the word (Horace's Siculique) is the same.
garde: nous auons en garde l'ame = 'we have the soul in keeping', echoed six words on by prins à garder and at the end by baillee en garde; gaide is no word.
balliee = baillée, 'delivered' (commise, & baillee en garde, the pair committed and delivered into keeping); ballice is no word, a misread of e as c.
